subject: TheraHealth long-document handling: truncation guardrails & eval brief
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@therahealth.com>, Carlos Reyes <c.reyes@therahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T15:12:00Z
Subject: TheraHealth discovery — long-doc requirements and next steps

Hi Marta / Carlos,

Thanks again for the call earlier — the product + clinical teams were really helpful in laying out the challenge. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get an evaluation running quickly: 

Summary of needs we captured:
- Summarization fidelity: you need extractive+abstractive summaries that preserve clinical assertions (medications, dosages, diagnoses) without hallucinations.
- Long documents: typical input is 8k–25k token patient records and discharge bundles; truncation at 4k caused missed facts in your pilot.
- Structured outputs: prefer a JSON manifest with sections (HPI, Meds, Allergies, Assessments) and confidence scores.
- PII/PHI handling: must support customer-managed KMS + clear audit logs per record.

What we propose as next steps:
1) We attached an evaluation plan (thera_eval_plan_v1.xlsx) and a prompt set (thera_prompt_set_v2.md). Please confirm the sample subset (we called out 200 records across 3 specialties).
2) Redwood recommendations to benchmark (shortlist): redwood-long-32k-v1 (quantized), rw-opt-32k-instruct, and a Llama-3-32k tuned variant. We recommend we run both full-token and chunk+memory pipelines to compare truncation vs summarization fidelity.
3) Pass/fail criteria: fact-level precision >= 95% for medication/dosage extraction; hallucination rate < 3% on randomized checks; summary coherence score (human) >= 4/5.
4) Timeline: if you sign off on the sample set by end of day Friday (11/19) we can return benchmark results and a short report by 11/27.

Open questions we need from you now:
- Confirm sample selection and whether we should de-id prior to upload (we can also do in-line PII redaction during eval if you prefer).
- Any additional MUST-HAVE extraction fields beyond the four sections above?
- Are there internal reviewers who should be on the evaluation report distribution (clinical lead + security)?

I'll loop Neha and Rishi for the technical runbook. Once you confirm samples we'll provision a secured S3 bucket and a dedicated evaluation job.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: thera_eval_plan_v1.xlsx (xlsx), thera_prompt_set_v2.md (md)

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@therahealth.com>

Date: 2026-11-15T09:07:00Z
Subject: Re: TheraHealth discovery — long-doc requirements and next steps

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We prefer that PII be removed before upload for the initial eval; can your team provide a de-id script or should we perform de-identification locally?
- Legal is looping in our privacy lead (legal@therahealth.com) to confirm the S3 setup and KMS flow. Could you send the SOC2 audit pointer and any relevant data retention options?
- The four sections you listed cover 90% of our needs; add a separate field for "Care Plan / Next Steps" if possible.

Timeline: we should be able to confirm sample selection by 11/18 EOD, and legal will try to expedite the KMS checklist by 11/20.

Also — regarding models — are these benchmarked with your quantized runtime already, or do you recommend a CPU fallback for some heavier sequences? We want to understand cost tradeoffs if we scale to nightly processing.

Best,
Marta
Director of Product | TheraHealth

Subject: Re: TheraHealth discovery — long-doc requirements and next steps

Marta — great questions, answers inline below and next actions at the bottom.

PII / De-id:
- For speed we recommend TheraHealth de-identify before upload for the formal eval; we included a lightweight de-id script in the Drive folder (link below). If you prefer, Redwood can run a redaction pass inside the secure eval bucket but that adds 1–2 days of setup.

SOC2 / Evidence:
- Attaching our SOC2 pointer in the Drive folder and will share the SOC2 summary PDF in the follow-up. For the eval we can provide per-request audit logs and an EV audit token to prove access controls.

Model and runtime notes (high-level):
- redwood-long-32k-v1 (quantized): best latency/throughput for large-context summarization; supports continuous KV cache and chunking strategies. Expect ~30% token-cost reduction vs baseline fp16 with our runtime.
- rw-opt-32k-instruct: strong instruction-following; slightly higher hallucination tendency on rare edge cases but good for structured extraction when combined with constrained decoding.
- llama-3-32k-ft: tuned on clinical examples for better entity preservation; may need more conservative temperature / sampling to reduce hallucinations.

Cost/backstop options:
- For heavy nightly pipelines we recommend model routing: run redwood-long-32k-v1 for summarization and fall back to a cheaper quantized opt model for cheaper rescoring/QA passes. We can include a simple cost-estimate table in the report.

Benchmark details we will run (these are in the eval plan):
- 200-record run across 3 specialties; metrics: entity-precision/recall, hallucination rate (manual adjudication sample), summary ROUGE/L, and human coherence rating.
- We will run both (1) single-shot full-context and (2) chunk+memory pipelines to compare truncation effects.

Requested internal action (assignments):
- Neha: please prepare the de-id helper and permissioned S3 + KMS setup (ETA 11/19).
- Rishi: prepare the evaluation harness and a small baseline run on a 50-doc sample (ETA 11/24).

Deliverables & timeline:
- Sign off on sample selection by TheraHealth: 11/18 EOD.
- Secure S3 + ingress: 11/20 (legal/infra checks).
- Baseline 50-doc run results: 11/24.
- Full 200-record report: 11/27.

Links / artifacts:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GkQj-thera-evals-2026
- Eval S3 (provisioned after sample sign-off): s3://redwood-evals/therahealth/long-doc
- HubSpot deal: HS-Deal-78921

Let me know if that schedule works and whether you want any changes to the pass/fail definitions.

Thanks,
Laura
